title: Kubernetes Administration (CKA)
subtitle: Install, secure, upgrade and troubleshoot Kubernetes clusters
audience_line: Engineers who run Kubernetes clusters and are preparing the CKA exam
overview: This programme prepares participants to administer Kubernetes clusters and to pass the Certified Kubernetes Administrator exam on its 2025 curriculum. They install a highly available cluster with kubeadm, upgrade it and back up etcd, secure it with RBAC and security contexts, control scheduling, configure cluster networking from the CNI to the Gateway API, manage storage, and extend the cluster with Helm, Kustomize, custom resources and operators. Troubleshooting runs through every phase, a timed mock exam measures readiness, and the programme closes with a final project: a cluster built, secured, upgraded and repaired by each team.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Engineers who run Kubernetes clusters and are preparing the CKA exam

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: Kubernetes user level (course: Docker & Kubernetes): Pods, Deployments, Services, Helm. Using Kubernetes is not taught again; this course is about running it

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 36 h: 30 h of chapters + 6 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures followed by guided labs at the command line; one timed mock exam

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs on premises: one lab server per team of two (64 GB RAM), provided by the organiser, hosting the Ubuntu virtual machines of each cluster (three control-plane nodes, two workers, a load balancer); open-source software only; no cloud account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: A lab validated at the end of each phase, a timed mock exam and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete the labs and the project

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can install, secure, upgrade, back up and troubleshoot a Kubernetes cluster from the command line and sit the CKA exam

phases.name: Cluster Installation & Lifecycle
phases.focus: kubeadm, highly available control plane, upgrades, etcd backup
phases.intro: Participants build a cluster the way the exam and production expect: a container runtime, kubeadm, a highly available control plane behind a load balancer. They then upgrade it one minor version and back up and restore etcd. Validated lab: a three-control-plane cluster upgraded without downtime, restored from an etcd snapshot.

chapters.title: Cluster Installation
chapters.content: kubeadm, highly available control plane, container runtime

chapters.title: Cluster Lifecycle
chapters.content: Version upgrades, etcd backup and restore

phases.name: Security & Scheduling
phases.focus: RBAC, ServiceAccounts, security contexts, scheduling controls
phases.intro: Participants grant each user and workload only the access it needs, run containers with restrictive security contexts, then decide where pods run with taints and tolerations, affinity, resource requests and priority classes. Validated lab: a team namespace with least-privilege RBAC, and a workload pinned to dedicated nodes that keeps priority under pressure.

chapters.title: Scheduling
chapters.content: Taints and tolerations, affinity, resource requests and limits, priority classes

phases.name: Networking, Storage & Extensions
phases.focus: CNI, Services and DNS, NetworkPolicies, Gateway API, storage, Helm, CRDs
phases.intro: Participants configure cluster networking from the CNI plugin to Services, CoreDNS, NetworkPolicies and the Gateway API, migrate an Ingress off the retired ingress-nginx, provision storage dynamically, and extend the cluster with Helm, Kustomize, custom resources and operators. Validated lab: an application reachable through the Gateway API, isolated by NetworkPolicies, with a dynamically provisioned volume.

chapters.title: Networking
chapters.content: CNI, Services, CoreDNS, NetworkPolicies, Gateway API, Ingress and migrating off ingress-nginx

chapters.title: Storage
chapters.content: PersistentVolumes and PersistentVolumeClaims, StorageClasses, dynamic provisioning

chapters.title: Extending Kubernetes
chapters.content: Helm, Kustomize, custom resource definitions and operators

phases.name: Troubleshooting & Exam Preparation
phases.focus: Node, pod and network troubleshooting, timed mock exam
phases.intro: Participants diagnose broken nodes, failing pods and network faults from logs, events and metrics, then sit a timed mock exam and learn the kubectl techniques that save time in a performance-based exam. Validated lab: a cluster with injected faults returned to a healthy state.

chapters.title: Troubleshooting
chapters.content: Nodes, pods, networking, logs and monitoring

chapters.title: Exam Preparation
chapters.content: Timed mock exam, kubectl speed techniques

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A highly available cluster, built, secured, upgraded and repaired
phases.intro: Each team builds a production-style cluster from a written brief on its lab server, reusing the phase labs, then repairs the faults injected by the trainer and presents its runbook.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Read the brief, build a highly available cluster with kubeadm, secure it with RBAC and NetworkPolicies

chapters.title: Operate & Document
chapters.content: Back up and restore etcd, upgrade the cluster, write the runbook

chapters.title: Fault Repair & Review
chapters.content: Fix the faults injected by the trainer; questions and feedback

project.title: A Production-Style Kubernetes Cluster
project.brief: A highly available cluster built with kubeadm, secured with RBAC and NetworkPolicies, backed up and restored from etcd, upgraded one minor version, and returned to health after faults injected by the trainer.
project.stack: Kubernetes, kubeadm, containerd, etcd, a CNI plugin, CoreDNS, Gateway API, Helm, Kustomize, kubectl
project.deliverable: Working cluster, runbook (install, backup, upgrade, recovery), fault report
